reviewer: Separate GPT-6.1 Sol visible-cue reviewer; automated browser assessment, not a human participant
build: Build09 forward phase-brake and central objective-marker offset, before parent followup layout/emissive/sign changes

ratings.reason: The successful approach now leaves the guard directly in front, making the three-second armor opening usable without a turn. I completed two visible-charge breaks and normal firing followups without enemy-position reads or arrangements. The second continuous attempt killed the guard without pausing between cue and followup. This is a concrete usability improvement. It does not validate blind player discovery, full-mission balance or enjoyment. The large floating instruction sign, highly blown-out white emitter forms, shared-courtyard structure and simple character art remain clear presentation/content limits.

methods: Installed Google Chrome headless through Playwright at1280x800, actual Three.js/WebGL render. No source edits.

All gameplay actions were deployment clicks, waiting for the rendered CHARGING label, normal W/Shift/RMB/LMB input, and synthetic mouse movement events handled by normal input listeners. No enemy coordinates, windup timers, teleporting, enemy deletion, resource changes or simulation stepping were used to decide actions.
captureState was sampled only after actions for reporting; it includes player/HUD statistics but was not used to locate or time enemies.

Attempt1 waited for first visible charge label, heldW+pressedShift, releasedW after250ms, captured actual image and paused. I used the image to choose an upward mouse adjustment for the visible upper optic, then resumed, aimed and fired450ms.
Attempt2 repeated that learned cue/approach/aim/fire sequence without pausing between charge cue and followup. It reused prior knowledge of the opening and the aiming adjustment.
Inspected actual phase-break and both post-followup screenshots via image viewer. Browser closed before reporting safe-to-edit.
verifiedImprovements: First visible-cue attempt produced1phaseInterrupt and left the warden in front of camera in the actual screenshot, instead of passing it behind.
Attempt1 followup yielded1criticalelimination,25magazine rounds,100health/60shield at4.3165 simulatedseconds.
Attempt2 continuous cue-to-followup sequence yielded1phaseInterrupt,1criticalelimination,25rounds,100health/60shield at3.5165 simulatedseconds; no pause between cue and kill.
THE HEART label is above the aiming region rather than on the upper optic in the inspected phase screenshot.

remainingFindings.finding: Upper optic and charge ring become nearly white solid forms under emissive lighting; their shape/weakpoint distinction is less clear than the amber-charge language suggests.
remainingFindings.recommendation: Tone down emissive output and preserve a distinct, smaller readable weakpoint while retaining the charge/break color vocabulary.

remainingFindings.finding: The large floating INDUCTION GUARD sign, shifted THE HEART label and mission announcement occupy the same upper central band in the phase screenshot.
remainingFindings.recommendation: Relocate or scale the sign as physical scenery and resolve marker/announcement layout without returning labels to the optic.

remainingFindings.finding: This review only exercised the opening and one enemy. It establishes an available repeatable approach-counter-followup path, not that humans want to use it or that all later encounters are equally readable.
remainingFindings.recommendation: Retain alternate tactics and collect later encounter and human evidence; do not raise damage solely because this automated sequence wins.

limitations: Prior context explicitly described the charge and phase-brake change; this is not blind discovery.
Automated visible-label reaction is faster/more consistent than many human responses.
First attempt paused after break for inspection; second reused its learned mouse adjustment.
Only opening success was tested, not full mission, replay variety, hardware performance, accessibility or auditory enjoyment.
Ratings are candid provisional agent judgments; no10/10, perfection or AAA-readiness claim.
